subject.title: fix(plugins): rebuild unverifiable managed npm installs

question: Should managed plugin reconciliation deliberately leave the prior installation quarantined and unavailable when rebuilding unverifiable lock state fails?
rationale: The code can safely implement either contract, but choosing integrity-first fail-closed behavior over restoring a previously working unverifiable tree is an operator-impact and upgrade-policy decision rather than a mechanical correctness question.

options.title: Approve fail-closed quarantine
options.body: Accept that failed rebuilding leaves the prior tree quarantined, provided the error clearly identifies the quarantine location and supported recovery action.

options.title: Restore on transient failure
options.body: Change rollback to reactivate the old tree after installation failure, preserving availability while knowingly retaining unverifiable integrity state.

options.title: Require explicit repair flow
options.body: Pause this runtime behavior and move stale-root rebuilding into an explicit doctor or operator-confirmed repair path.

recommendation.title: Approve fail-closed quarantine
recommendation.body: Accept that failed rebuilding leaves the prior tree quarantined, provided the error clearly identifies the quarantine location and supported recovery action.
